role: Data Engineer, Analytics Engineering (Senior Analytics Engineer)

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Define and implement data quality checks, SLAs, and governance practices so that our data is accurate, reliable, and compliant
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Rigour signals (data quality, governance, SLAs, compliance, testing) dominate throughout with no velocity/speed language present.
evidence.domain_risk: keeping our customers, and the bank's data, safe and secure... so that our data is accurate, reliable, and compliant
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: NatWest is a regulated bank and the role explicitly serves Private Banking & Wealth Management with compliance language directly present, placing it firmly at high domain risk.
evidence.data_team_maturity: We're building a brand new Data Products factory capability at the Private Banking & Wealth Management (PBWM) franchise
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: The Data Products factory itself is explicitly brand new ('building a brand new... capability', 'from the ground up') even though it sits within a large, established bank, giving a genuinely mixed early/mature signal.
evidence.jd_authorship: Design and evolve standardised, cross domain data models such as party, account, deposit, mortgages that align with our enterprise data model
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Responsibilities name precise domain entities (party, account, deposit, mortgages) and specific technical formats (iceberg on AWS), showing a hiring manager who knows the actual data model.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: shape the canonical and semantic data layers that power our Analytics, AI, reporting, and self service capabilities... for the Private Banking & Wealth Management (PBWM) franchise
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The role is explicitly built around a Private Banking & Wealth Management business, with data quality tied to compliance and accurate financial entity modelling, decisively finance-oriented.
evidence.autonomy_level: This is a hands on role with significant influence over how data is structured, governed, and consumed across PBWM
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The JD explicitly grants significant influence and ownership over data structure and governance decisions, a strategic framing reinforced by 'design clean, reusable data assets from the ground up'.
evidence.ai_role: shape the canonical and semantic data layers that power our Analytics, AI, reporting, and self service capabilities
evidence.ai_role_explanation: The candidate builds canonical/semantic data infrastructure that downstream AI capabilities consume, placing this as ai_enabler.
evidence.testing_framing: Define and implement data quality checks, SLAs, and governance practices so that our data is accurate, reliable, and compliant
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Data quality and governance are framed as something the candidate defines and implements, an ownership responsibility, not a listed tool.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: keeping our customers, and the bank's data, safe and secure... so that our data is accurate, reliable, and compliant
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: High: compliance and data safety/security language appears early in the role summary and recurs throughout, reflecting fear of bad or non-compliant data reaching a regulated banking business.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: partnering with Business, Technology and Functions to design clean, reusable data assets from the ground up
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Explicit 'from the ground up' and 'brand new... capability' language indicate the dominant framing is building new infrastructure rather than fixing/scaling existing systems.
evidence.loss_aversion: so that our data is accurate, reliable, and compliant — compliance and trustworthiness are framed as core to the role at a regulated bank, not secondary operational concerns.
